name: cobblers

rescaled_from.note: Vertical rescale, option B: identity at or below y145, gain rising to 5 over a 55-block blend, so the peak goes y200 to y310 and the world tree reads 1.73x the tallest mountain instead of 2.67x. The gain is applied to the smoothed LANDFORM, not per column: per column it multiplies local relief too, and the largest adjacent step went 22.8 to 96.8 blocks, one-column walls rather than mountains. Quantisation is floor-preserving, so 0 columns at or below y145 change integer elevation; the nearest-value quantiser moved 48,568 of them. docs/world-building/VERTICAL_RESCALE.md

sculpted_from.note: Local brushes on the river cut: coasts by class, massif asymmetry and summits, volcano cones, hillside relief against contour rings. Protected sites, river channels and lake basins keep their columns (checked: lake basins 0 changed, river water under 0.003 blocks, settlement footprints 0). docs/world-building/SCULPT.md

derived_from.generator: python tools/grade_rivers.py plan && python tools/grade_rivers.py cut --replace
derived_from.note: The authored heightmap. Rivers are planned on it (data/rivers.json computed_from_sha256) and cut into the imported file, which is regenerated, never edited. Terrain edits go into this file, then plan and cut again.

heightmap.revision_note: 2026-09-16 (vertical rescale, option B): mountains raised without moving anything built. The elevation curve is the identity at or below y145 and gains to 5x over a 55-block blend, taking the peak y200 to y310, relief above y145 from 55 to 165 blocks, and massif slope above y145 from p90 0.390 to 0.854 (7.5 percent of that ground now over 45 degrees, from 0). y145 is where six independent constraints sit: the highest elder tree y144.4, the highest water y127.0, the cavern surface y134.7, the grove y114.9-118.1, the ridge governing the Pallet sightline y139.0, and the p90 of land elevation y144.14. 0 columns at or below y145 change integer elevation. 2026-09-15 (fourth, not exported): the major river starts where its path first runs between valley walls (10 blocks within 250 on both sides, three samples 48 apart), 817 blocks down the path at (3136, 1636) on the Glacial Tear trough floor, restoring the trough creek; the lower river keeps its original course (within 2 blocks) and reaches. Rivers cut f5ff054e. Previous files in cobblers-server-retired/2026-09-15-valley-head-files/. 2026-09-15 (third): the major river starts where its path first drains 0.13 km2, in the Glacial Tear valley at (3732, 2232), not 1,661 blocks higher on the flank above Merian, where the cut ran along the mountainside and straight across the plain (tools/grade_rivers.py HEAD_KM2); rivers re-cut (6b6352bc) and the sculpt re-applied; relief noise now normalised independently of terrain so edits stay local. Previous files in cobblers-server-retired/2026-09-15-river-head/. 2026-09-15 (second): hillside relief added to the sculpt (data/sculpt.json relief): amplitude 10 x regional grade, capped at 2.5 blocks, stretched down the fall line, so contour rings break into spurs and gullies; largest change 4.9 blocks; footprints, basins, channels and the hometown area unchanged. The previous sculpt file land_8k_16_sculpted.png stays beside it. 2026-09-15: the import is the sculpted derivative of the river cut: coasts by class, massif asymmetry and summits, volcano cones (tools/sculpt.py).2026-09-14 (third): the tarn at the head of the ravine above Peak Pond became a lake (level 127) with a graded outflow to the north coast; 2,786 columns changed, nothing raised. The previous cut file is in cobblers-server-retired/2026-09-14-tarn/. 2026-09-14 (second): the import is now the river-cut derivative of the hand-carved revision: graded lake outflows and rivers with catchment-sized channels, and the major river's valley (docs/world-building/RIVERS.md). Earlier the same day: hand-carved revision (glacier, rift, lakes, rivers) saved as land_8k_16_eroded.png; the file before that survives as land_8k_16_eroded.png.bak and its annotation as land_8k_16_eroded_annotated_outdated.png.

import.line_note: The same straight line as the first import (40/255 -> y40, 254/255 -> y200), extended down to full-scale 0 -> y10.093458. Land is unchanged; only sea columns below y40 deepen (docs/world-building/OCEAN.md). Approved 2026-09-13.

export.name: cobblers-10240

worldpainter_levels.note: WorldPainter world levels are whole numbers, so low_out 10.093458 is written as an image level below zero. The line is now 0 -> y10.093458, 65278 -> y310, i.e. 0.004594373 blocks an image level, so y10 falls at image level -20.342 (it was -32.125 when the line topped out at y200). Same construction, new slope.

export.buffer_note: 1024 blocks of ocean inside the border plus a 256-block ring outside it. The ring is never reachable; it exists so chunks loaded within view distance of the border are already written and nothing generates outside the border.
export.seed_policy: Carried from the previous world's level.dat. Not committed: the public repo records only its sha256.
export.worldpainter_project_sha256_measured: 2026-09-17, file saved 2026-09-16 08:05 after the thinned-grass paint; previous values cd6439ea (2026-09-15 export) and 47e01a6f (docs/STATE.md, 2026-09-16) are superseded

painted.maps: tools/paint_maps.py from data/regions.json paint_presets (with scree), data/landmarks.json water bodies and ravines, data/rivers.json graded courses (per-column water levels, bed material, river biome), shore materials by coast class (build/sculpt/coast_class.png), and data/foliage.json forests: 77,750 custom objects from kits/structures/foliage at computed positions, including five landmark trees
painted.note: Paint on the sculpted heightmap. See docs/world-building/REEXPORT.md for the export and its known issues.

export.worldpainter_project_note: Beside the heightmap under source_root. Painting starts from this file; its hash changes when it is saved again.
export.measured_ceiling_note: Terrain only, measured 2026-09-17 on the canonical heightmap (sha256 3eb0edee) through worldpainter_levels: the highest value is 65276, under image_high 65278, so it maps to y309.99 and 0 columns exceed the top of the line. The pre-rescale value was y201 (source values above 65406 overshooting a y200 line). Built structures are not terrain and are measured separately: see built_ceiling.

built_ceiling.what: the world tree at Foothill Woods, trunk centre (2016, 2280), ground y116, 418 blocks tall
built_ceiling.measured_from: tools/world_tree.py output (derived/sites/world_tree_foothill_woods.json top_y): the placed block list, not the heightmap and not a world read
built_ceiling.runtime_limit: y-64..575 from modpack/datapacks/cobblers_height (dimension_type height 640, min_y -64); the crown is 40 blocks under it

verified.note: Re-measured on the 2026-09-14 hand-carved revision. The largest steps (3-4 blocks) are pixel-stepped terraces on the carved basin walls around Lake Tilpey and the glacier mouth.

rejected_artifacts.reason: sawtooth wraparound across the surface; 7.3% of horizontally adjacent pixels differed by >100 blocks; stored as 8-bit RGB with height only in the red channel
landmass clipped to 255 (mean 244, median 255); no land elevation data

notes: Grid origin confirmed as corner-at-origin, A1 at block 0,0, spanning 0-8191 on both axes.
bounds are derived from grid origin + cell_size * columns/rows and are not authored by hand.

import.low_in/high_in are fractions of full scale, so they survive a bit-depth change. Tooling multiplies by (2**bit_depth - 1) at read time. They were originally authored as 40 and 254 against an 8-bit file, which is where 0.156863 and 0.996078 come from.
import.low_out/high_out/water_level are absolute Minecraft Y values and never scale.

source_root is machine-specific and is not committed. On the authoring machine the heightmap and its provenance files sit directly in the Documents folder; set COBBLERS_SOURCE_ROOT or pass --source-root. See data/notes/source_tree.md.

The server world cobblers-10240 is exported from this heightmap by tools/reexport.py (2026-09-13). The previous world erosion-land-8k came from the rejected erosion_land_8k.png and was retired with its Distant Horizons LOD stores.
grid and bounds describe the landmass heightmap only; the exported world is larger (export.canvas) and the world border sits between the two (export.border).
